blocks.text: In sp3 hybridization one s orbital (low energy, spherical) and three p orbitals (higher energy, dumb-bell shaped) intermix to give a new set of four orbitals of the same energy and shape, each an sp3 hybrid orbital, arranged in a tetrahedral geometry as in CH4. Carbon in its ground state is 2s2 2px1 2py1; in the excited state one 2s electron is promoted, giving 2s1 2px1 2py1 2pz1; the four outermost orbitals then mix into four sp3 hybrids, each with one electron. The energies of hybrid orbitals are lower than those of the unhybridized p orbitals. Each sp3 hybrid has two lobes, one larger and one smaller; for simplicity the smaller lobe is usually not shown. The four hybrids of equal energy have a tetrahedral geometry with the carbon nucleus at the centre. Methane is formed by the overlap of the sp3 hybrids with the 1s orbitals of four hydrogen atoms, four sigma bonds from sp3-s overlap directed towards the corners of a regular tetrahedron.

In sp2 hybridization one s and two p orbitals of an atom intermix to form three sp2 hybrid orbitals. The three half-filled sp2 hybrids are arranged in a trigonal planar geometry with bond angles of 120 degrees. This explains the geometry of planar molecules such as BF3. Boron is 2s2 2px1 in the ground state; excited, it is 2s1 2px1 2py1; the three outermost orbitals mix to give three sp2 hybrids. One p orbital of fluorine is half-filled (say 2pz), and BF3 is formed by the overlap of the three half-filled sp2 hybrids of boron with the 2pz orbitals of three fluorine atoms; the structure is trigonal planar with bond angles of 120 degrees.

In sp hybridization one s orbital (low energy, spherical) and one p orbital (high energy, dumb-bell shaped) intermix to give two orbitals of the same energy and shape, the sp hybrids, arranged linearly at 180 degrees. Beryllium is 2s2 in the ground state; excited, it is 2s1 2px1; the two mix into two sp hybrids that lie in a line. This explains the geometry of linear molecules such as beryllium chloride, BeCl2, formed when the two sp hybrids of beryllium overlap the half-filled p orbitals of two chlorine atoms.

blocks.alt: Three bands. Each shows box diagrams of the ground, excited and hybridized valence shell of an atom with green hybrid boxes, and a flat drawing of the molecule: carbon's four sp3 lobes to four hydrogens in a tetrahedron, boron's three sp2 lobes to three fluorines in a triangle, and beryllium's two sp lobes to two chlorines in a line. A summary box lists the three types.
blocks.caption: sp3, sp2 and sp hybridization of carbon, boron and beryllium (original diagram after Figures 3.27 to 3.32 and the printed box diagrams).
blocks.long_description: Carbon promotes one 2s electron, then mixes 2s with three 2p into four equal sp3 hybrids pointing to the corners of a tetrahedron at 109.5 degrees; each overlaps a hydrogen 1s to make methane. Boron mixes 2s with two 2p into three sp2 hybrids at 120 degrees in a plane, leaving one p orbital empty, and bonds three fluorine 2p orbitals in BF3. Beryllium mixes 2s with one 2p into two sp hybrids at 180 degrees, leaving two p orbitals, and bonds two chlorine p orbitals in BeCl2. The hybrids share one energy, between s and p, and the number of hybrids equals the number of orbitals mixed.
